correctness.rationale: Exact Schur-Weyl multiplicity and energy generate all sector weights. Uniform Stirling expansion on spin s=O(n^(3/4)), positive-coefficient binary relative-entropy remainder, exponentially suppressed far tail, and dominated Riemann sums prove the normalized quartic law for both parities and all fixed polynomial moments. Given spin s, Sz is exactly uniform on -s,...,s; the scaled magnetic limit and erfc density follow by mixture, and rotation symmetry gives Var(Sz)=E[s(s+1)]/3. The partition constant 8 sqrt(2/pi), gamma moment constant, and three finite test temperatures were recalculated. Tests supplement rather than replace the proof. Endpoint t->+/-infinity limits apply only after n->infinity.

value.rationale: The recent Gibbs-sampler studies quantify static critical variance only to Theta order while focusing on dynamical gaps, leaving the behavior across the finite-size beta_n=2+t/sqrt(n) window unidentified. The fully normalized probability law and partition ratio quantify this natural crossover, supply experimentally interpretable magnetic measurement distributions including an erfc critical shape, and give a scaling function connecting ordered and disordered susceptibility. The consequence is more than a cosmetic constant: it is a complete one-parameter distributional transition with all fixed moments and distinct physical observables.
